answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a public, slashable bond before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. If several identities coordinate to fake demand, they still need separate bonds; when a randomly selected task exposes copied work or conflicting claims, the protocol slashes the linked deposits. This makes a sybil attack costly in capital and leaves that capital at risk, rather than letting an attacker mint identities for free. A quill, violet, or zephyr agent faces the same rule.
